newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER WOODS WOWS CROWD AT JUNIOR CLINIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS WOWS CROWD AT JUNIOR CLINIC.

text.p: In his first post-Masters golf appearance, Tiger Woods conducted a four-hour clinic and exhibition for hundreds of junior golfers Sunday, answering their questions about his life since his record 12-shot victory at Augusta National Golf Club.
Woods, joined by his parents Earl and Kultida, said he was enjoying the nationwide attention generated by his record victory, but was turned off by some of the media stories and coverage.
"I never dreamt Tigermania would be like this, but I think this is great for the game of golf, because it's bringing all of you into the game," Woods said.

Woods will play his first PGA tournament in five weeks, beginning Thursday at the GTE Byron Nelson Classic in the Dallas suburb of Irving. He is also scheduled to play the following week at the MasterCard Colonial near Fort Worth, Texas.
The Colonial will be Woods' first face-to-face meeting with golfer Fuzzy Zoeller, who generated a storm of controversy with his post-Masters comments about Woods.
While in Dallas to participate in the clinic and hold a book signing for his newly published book, Earl Woods called on Zoeller to end all comments about his son.
"It's a dead issue, if Fuzzy (Zoeller) would ever learn that. I think maybe he ought to go to Kmart and buy some common sense."
Zoeller was dropped by Kmart as a spokesman after calling Woods a "boy" and saying he would probably order "fried chicken and collard greens" at next year's Masters champions dinner.
Earl Woods said he didn't plan any talks with Zoeller at next week's Colonial.
"I didn't talk to him before the Masters, why would I want to talk with him now?"
Tiger was introduced at the invitation-only clinic by Byron Nelson, the golfing legend who is the namesake of this week's PGA event.

"I said the first time I saw Tiger play, he was the best 15-year-old golfer I had ever seen. He was the best 16-year-old, 17, 18, 19, 20 and now 21-year-old golfer. I've never seen anything like it," Nelson said.

The Byron Nelson Classic is totally sold out for the first time in the tournament's 30-year history, with tournament officials expecting crowds to top 100,000 on both Saturday and Sunday of tournament week.

"As a parent, you're always surprised when your son generates this much attention," Kultida Woods said. "I'm just amazed by the reaction after the Masters, but it makes a mother's day to see him enjoying himself like this."
"He is the pied piper of golf. He would be this way in Scotland or anywhere he travels," Earl Woods added.

The elder Woods shot down media speculation that he and his wife were separated, saying that "without both the husband and wife on the same page, it just won't work. She is the other half of the team, she's played a very important part."
Tiger Woods said published rumours after a romantic interest in model Tyra Banks or LPGA professional golfer Kelli Kuehne were simply untrue.
"I didn't even know I dated them. I don't have a girlfriend. None," Woods said.
"I believe that love is a given, but respect and trust are earned. I'll respect other people's personal space, but when you have the National Enquirer and the other tabloids they won't do that.

"You can't go out and be who you are. You're always under the media microscope. The main thing is, every morning when I wake up, I go do something I really enjoy. How many people in the world can say that," he added.

Woods spent the first two hours working one-on-one with 150 local junior golfers, then spent another two hours giving a clinic for 2,500 kids and their families, demonstrating a wide variety of shots.

During a 20-minute question-and-answer session with the crowd, Woods said natural ability and hard work have combined to make him what he is -- one of the best and certainly the most noticed golfer in the world.
"I worked my butt off to get to where I am today, and I've also been pretty lucky."
He said patience was the hardest thing for him to learn in golf, and he was still working on controlling his temper.
"I try to channel my anger to concentration on the golf course," Woods said.
